Hi Samira / Tom — thanks for the notes. I’m Priyom from our security/infra team; happy to be the technical lead for the intake. Answers below are intended to be an initial summary we can put into the SIG Lite/CAIQ starter: 

1) Data persistence and caching
- We do not persist raw prompts in plaintext. Production prompt input and generated responses are written to ephemeral service logs for troubleshooting and are deleted according to customer-configured retention policies.
- KV cache is used to accelerate inference; cached state is scoped per session and is stored in our GPU-backed cache in the same cloud region as the inference workload (US regions for MedAlign). See attached kv-cache-residency.txt (stub) for locations.

2) Encryption & keys
- Data at rest: platform storage is encrypted using AES-256. For enterprise/private customers we offer customer-managed KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) — we can enable a dedicated customer key for MedAlign.
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ with forward secrecy for all public endpoints.

3) PHI handling / endpoints
- PHI is only processed by the inference service in the customer’s selected region. We will map PHI processing to specific endpoints in the high-level-dataflow.pdf (stub) attached.
- Access controls: role-based access with logged access events; we can provide an access control matrix and example audit log excerpts if required during review.

Attachments included (initial): high-level-dataflow.pdf (stub), kv-cache-residency.txt (stub), SOC2-report-2027-TypeII.pdf (stub), network-diagram-v2.png (stub). We’ll redact any customer identifiers before sharing.

Next steps we propose:
- We will prefill SIG Lite + CAIQ answers and return the initial package within 5 business days (target 2028-04-23).
- Schedule a 30-minute evidence run-through — Kimberly will send a Calendly link; we’re available 2028-04-18 afternoon.
- Prepare draft BAA and share with Tom for legal review in parallel (Kimberly to own).

If you want more technical artifacts immediately, tell us which items your reviewers prioritize and we’ll surface those first.
